summary: Wesson Coulomb logarithm estimate for the declared collision pair.

capability: Wesson Coulomb logarithm ln Lambda for electron-ion collisions from temperature in keV and density in m^-3.
operation: Evaluate the Wesson electron-ion Coulomb logarithm
discovery.model: Wesson Coulomb-log relation ln Lambda = 31.3 - 0.5 ln(n_e) + ln(1000 T_e) with explicit numeric boundary checks.
discovery.geometry: Homogeneous plasma point with broadcast T_e and n_e arrays; no spatial geometry is inferred.
discovery.boundary: T_e in keV and n_e in m^-3 must be finite and strictly positive.

identity.definition: 31.3-0.5*ln(n_e)+ln(1000*T_e); keV is converted to eV by the factor 1000. Evaluation uses ln(1000)+ln(T), avoiding intermediate overflow/underflow.
identity.model: Wesson Coulomb-log relation with explicit SciRel numeric boundary checks
identity.boundary: strictly positive finite T_e in keV and n_e in m^-3
assumptions: This is a mathematical weak-coupling estimate.
The caller decides whether a positive/adequate Coulomb logarithm is physically applicable.

inputs.name: T_e
inputs.dtype: real integer/float numeric scalar or array-like; converted to float64
inputs.constraints: finite and strictly positive; nonempty, boolean/string/complex/masked values rejected

inputs.name: n_e
inputs.dtype: real integer/float numeric scalar or array-like; converted to float64
inputs.constraints: finite and strictly positive; nonempty, boolean/string/complex/masked values rejected

outputs.name: result
outputs.constraints: Finite signed mathematical formula value; physical suitability for a collision model is caller-owned.

preconditions: strictly positive finite T_e in keV and n_e in m^-3

Above 10 eV the caller accepts the high-temperature (quantum cutoff) branch: the relation is the quantum-cutoff form for T_e > 10 Z^2 eV, which is 10 eV at Z = 1 for this signature, and warns below it. The provenance of the 10 Z^2 eV boundary is NOT verified against an original source (UNKNOWN).
supported: Finite NumPy evaluation of the declared relation and broadcast shape on the quantum-cutoff branch, valid above the declared T_e ~ 10 Z^2 eV boundary (10 eV here; boundary provenance UNKNOWN).
excluded: Whole-transport evolution, experimental calibration, and implicit coordinate reconstruction.
Interpreting zero or negative computed logarithms as valid weakly coupled collision physics; physical calibration or a regime-switching model.

The low-temperature electron-ion classical-cutoff branch (a classical-cutoff form 23 - ln(n_e^0.5 Z T_e^-1.5), T_e in eV, n_e in cm^-3; source provenance pending, UNKNOWN) is not provided: below 10 eV the returned quantum-branch value only warns, and it sits above that form by about +37% at n_e = 1e17 m^-3, +55.5% at 1e19 and +112% at 1e21 (0.1 eV; the gap grows with density). The two forms cross near 16.2 eV, above which the quantum form reads lower.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for boolean/string/complex/masked or empty input, non-finite values, malformed or incompatible shape, and the nonpositive or singular domains named by the callable contract.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises FloatingPointError if accepted finite inputs produce an unrepresentable output; no fallback is returned. Emits scirel.ApplicabilityWarning when any input temperature is below 10 eV, the declared boundary for the quantum branch at Z = 1 (provenance UNKNOWN); the value is returned unchanged.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this is a direct algebraic mapping.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No output is returned after an exception.

example.description: Run the relation on a finite declared-domain case.
example.code:
import warnings
import numpy as np
from scirel.physics import calculate_log_lambda_ei
r=calculate_log_lambda_ei(2., 1e19)
assert np.isfinite(r)
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    low = calculate_log_lambda_ei(0.005, 1e19)
assert np.isfinite(low) and len(caught) == 1
example.expected: A finite Coulomb logarithm for the in-range sample, plus one ApplicabilityWarning for the below-10-eV sample whose value is returned unchanged.

scope: Independent 60-digit Decimal logarithms over temperature/density/charge scales including smallest subnormal and largest float64; transformation/scaling identities.
Declared failure cases for empty, boolean/string/complex/masked, nonfinite and incompatible inputs.
Agreement with the canonical SciRel callers and dependencies of this relation.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Maintained tests establish the named relation, shape and selected boundary behavior only; they do not establish global physical calibration.
known_limitations: No external calibration or collision-frequency composition is claimed.
Only the Wesson algebra and declared numerical boundaries are covered.
Sauter et al. (1999) use this form (31.3 - ln(sqrt(n_e)/T_e[eV]), with T in keV here) as lnLambda_e in the electron collisionality nu*_e; the 'ee' function (constant 31.0) is a different estimate.

The low-temperature regime below the declared boundary T_e ~ 10 Z^2 eV (boundary provenance UNKNOWN) is not represented: a classical-cutoff electron-ion form (23 - ln(n_e^0.5 Z T_e^-1.5), T_e in eV and n_e in cm^-3; source provenance pending, UNKNOWN) is a separate relation, so the returned quantum-branch value only warns. Relative to that form the returned value is about +37% at 0.1 eV for n_e = 1e17 m^-3, +55.5% at 1e19 and +112% at 1e21 (the gap grows with density because the fixed absolute offset is divided by a smaller logarithm), and the two forms cross near 16.2 eV, above which the quantum form reads lower; the boundary is therefore not a 'below is wrong, above is right' rule. The warning computes this deviation at the caller's own sample instead of quoting a fixed percentage.
